summary.intent: Redesign the Ask Soony main view (launch timeline, two-pane decision UI, visual identity) for a hackathon demo, make the system generalize beyond the Soony case via a generic paper check agent, and get a professional-looking design artifact to evaluate.
summary.outcome: The launch timeline and backend clock were built (185 tests passing) and the main-view builder finished; the paper check agent and identity alternative B are still running. The user rejected the first style-guide proposal as unprofessional, so a Design-type artifact with high-fidelity screens was started. A test run was failing at the end while checking the combined changes.

repo: Live server on :8000 does not hot-reload Python; it must be restarted for backend changes (e.g. the new `clock` in /api/state) to appear.
Challenge rules forbid hardcoding fixes or overfitting to specific events, so demo cards must come from generic detection rather than curated document references in scripts/demo_cards.py.
Edition copies-at-risk is the max (not sum) of open cards' figures since every box needs all parts; cards counted in parts are excluded.
launch_status.xlsx is titled 'Saturday 13:00' and must be treated as a snapshot time (packed_as_of), not as current.
Card fields arrives_at and part_name are derived from finding text and components.csv rather than hardcoded ids.
Parallel builders were split by file ownership (api.py/UI vs papercheck.py/demo_cards.py/background.py) to avoid edit conflicts.

code.finding: Clock logic: pack clock uses the time each packed count was taken, a past stop stays fixed instead of moving to now on each 5 s poll, and fallback shifts are used only when no plan states any.
One assertion changed (250 to 300) to enforce 'never below an open card's figure' for edition copies at risk.

workflow: Splitting work across parallel agent builders with disjoint file sets lets independent features progress simultaneously.
Rendering UI via a standalone harness at different fake times (now, Sun 14:00, Sat 15:00) gives reviewable screenshots of time-dependent views.
A Design-type Artifact (artboards) suits high-fidelity UI comparison better than an HTML style-guide page.

friction: The assistant mistook an image-size note from its own screenshot read for a user message and had to apologize.
The first visual identity proposal (A) was judged unprofessional by the user, with the overall design the main issue.
The timeline shows a sea of red because the verifier's 34,800 Standard shortfall likely ignores the 28,000 Hwaseong cards already received.
A test failed in the final combined run (papercheck WIP excluded) and was still being investigated.
open_items: Verify and correct the 34,800 Game Card shortfall at the source before letting the timeline declare Standard stopped.
Finish and review the paper check agent, then verify it re-finds Hwaseong, PackRight rev B, the statues and the art books on its own.
Publish identity alternative B and the high-fidelity Design artifact, then have the user choose a direction.
Run the visual-identity pass across all screens (main view, Routines, /d/<id>, login, evidence, phone, PWA icon, Teams card).
Make the deadline concept configurable (deadline, products, capacity) instead of Soony-specific naming.
Fix the failing test, then do final screenshot review and commit; nothing from the timeline builder is committed yet.
